text:
maria: Heads-up — after the runtime push last night I'm seeing a surge of OOM throttles on a subset of p100 nodes. Not full outages but lots of evictions and batch rejections. Anyone else seeing this?
perf-bot: automated-alert: OOM_EVICTIONS increased ~3x since 3337776000. sparkline: ▇▇▇▇▇ Links: http://perf/reports/3337778888/flame (flamegraph) :warning:
liam: saw it. quick skim of the flame suggests batching is assembling larger token aggregates when KV miss rate spikes. more tokens => larger KV working set per batch.
sophia: did we change kernel selection heuristics in the last deploy? iirc we preferred fused-attn for seqs >= 1024 which could inflate intermediary buffers.
raj: we did flip a fastpath to favor the fused kernel when seq_dist mean > 900 (deployed in 3337776000). the kernel has slightly higher scratch allocation on p100s.
jen: mitigation idea: lower batch token_budget_target on p100/generic nodes from 4096 -> 2048 to reduce per-batch kv footprint. quick config tweak can test if evictions drop.
liam: +1. also switch the admission policy for the broker from `bytes_only` to `pressure_signal` so admission accounts for live KV memory pressure, not just queued bytes.
maria: sounds reasonable — what's the perf tradeoff on tail latency?
sophia: small regress on 95/99 for short reqs (10-30ms) but OOMs/kills cause much worse tails. prefer stable.
liam: proposed patch (pseudo):
```yaml
batch_broker:
  token_budget_target: 2048
  admit_policy: pressure_signal
  pressure_signal:
    kv_pressure_threshold: 0.8
    ewma_alpha: 0.2
kernel_selection:
  fused_attn_seq_threshold: 1200  # raise to avoid hitting fused path too early on p100
```
jen: i'll canary this in staging and run the replay for an hour.
raj: how do we compute `kv_pressure` in practice? is it just allocated / capacity?
liam: yes, simple marker: pressure = kv_allocated_bytes / kv_capacity_bytes. smooth with ewma so short spikes don't throttle aggressively. Also expose per-batch `kv_delta` metric.
maria: add admit_reason tag to each rejected request so we can see "pressure" vs "queue_full" vs "kernel_mismatch" in dashboards.
sophia: also let's add a small "breather slot" mechanic: when pressure > 0.9 stop new long-seq batches for X ms to let eviction complete. it's less disruptive than whole-node backoff.
perf-bot: queued perf-snapshot job 4523 (staging canary). will publish flame/diff once done.
raj: PR opened D1234 with the config change + admit tagging. i'll link test artifacts here once CI finishes.
liam: if canary looks good we roll to p100 pool only first, monitor kv_evictions and tail latency for 30m, then expand.
jen: on it — canary start @3337779000. will post results. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks team. main goals: stop OOM evictions, preserve overall throughput, and instrument reasons so we can refine dynamically.
